name: Lost River Range High Traverse

legs.route: Chicken-Out Ridge from the standard trailhead

legs.connect: Follow the ridge with exposed class 4 scrambling on good rock; drop by a scree and slab chute to the big saddle.
Cross the saddle to the base of Idaho; steep on every side, with some class 4 to low class 5.

legs.route: South ridge of Idaho, then the pinnacled crest
legs.connect: Mostly class 4 to 5 on the crest; class 3 ground exists on the west side. Water is scarce on this stretch.
Continue along the crest toward Leatherman Pass; the descent off the far side is steep and loose.
Class 3 ridge; the far side is as unpleasant as Leatherman's.

legs.route: Church by the west or north face from the tarn basin; Donaldson by the connecting ridge
legs.connect: Bypass the rotten towers on the ridge from Bad Rock by going round the west face to the tarn between the two peaks.
Class 3 and rotten, with a cliff to bypass. Breitenbach and Lost River Mountain beyond are extras.

how: A full-range alpine scramble along the crest from Borah. Climbers carry food and camp gear and stash water, because the high ridge has almost none apart from a spring near Leatherman Pass, a tarn by Church and a few snow patches. Most of it is class 3 to 4 with short class 5 steps and rotten rock; one party roped four pitches on Church's north face while another walked round the west side. Rappel gear is useful on the later ridges.
descent: Leave by a canyon drainage on the east side, down-climbing short cliffs and waterfalls, then walk the plain back to the road; a bike or second vehicle shortens the road section.
logistics: Late summer, after the snow has thinned, starting from the Borah trailhead. A bike or shuttle car is needed at the far end. Carry a helmet, a short rope, and water for the dry stretches.
notes: Only two first-hand accounts read, both on the same guidebook site (different authors and years, same line). They differ on the finish: one ends at No Regret and a canyon descent, the other continues over Breitenbach to Lost River Mountain. Not a crowded objective.

name: Mount Church and Donaldson Peak

legs.route: Headwall from the tarn to the Church/Donaldson col, then the east ridge

legs.connect: Return along the airy east ridge to the col, then climb the short slabby ridge to Donaldson.

how: Both peaks share one approach: up the north fork of Jones Creek to a tarn, then a loose headwall to the col between them. From there the east ridge to Church involves exposed walking with route-finding to avoid steep downclimbs, and Donaldson is a short scramble above the col. Plan on 11 or more hours and wear a helmet on the loose headwall.
descent: Return over the col and down the same headwall and scree to the tarn, then follow the canyon trail out; the lower trail is easy to lose.
logistics: The trailhead is off Lone Cedar Creek Road near Mackay; high clearance is advised. Water at the tarn is poor, so bring a filter or carry extra. Snow on the ridge in autumn has turned parties back.
notes: Guide update says Donaldson's northeast ridge is class 3; no class given for Church's east ridge in any source.
